_comment: Lexical (regex, comment-stripped) and structural (path) checks. Syntax-tree checks now exist too, but are code-driven (see code_checks.py, registered via @register) rather than declared here -- route-graph checks still don't exist (needs its own research pass on Metro internals, see git history). Every check here is skill-agnostic; skill_map.json is the only file that says which skill(s) currently claim a given check. See SKILL_UPTAKE_COVERAGE_ANALYSIS.md (repo root, untracked) for the full-ecosystem gap analysis this file's expo-native-ui/expo-ui/expo-data-fetching/expo-dom/expo-tailwind-setup/eas-hosting/expo-app-clip checks and the expo-router/expo-project-structure gap-fill checks came from.

checks.description: Imports from 'expo-router' at all

Uses a real expo-router navigation API -- declarative (<Link>, <Redirect>) or imperative (useRouter/useLocalSearchParams/useSegments/usePathname/useNavigation) -- all are valid per the skill, not just the <Link> tag. Verified against a real authored app that legitimately uses only useRouter().

Uses a real Stack/Tabs/NativeTabs/Drawer/Slot JSX element, not a bare word match. Drawer confirmed necessary against a real wiki_reader app using expo-router/drawer -- a Stack/Tabs/NativeTabs-only list would have false-negatived on legitimate code.
SDK 56+ rule: never import @react-navigation/* directly -- use expo-router/react-navigation instead
app/ (or src/app/) directory exists

At least one index route exists (proxy for 'the app always has a route matching /'). Known limitation: matches any index.* anywhere under app/, not specifically the root -- an app with only a nested index (e.g. app/settings/index.tsx) and no real root route would still pass. Verified correct on 2 real apps using route groups ((tabs)/index.tsx, (drawer)/index.tsx), since groups don't affect the URL path -- but this is a proxy, not a real route-graph check (deferred, see uptake_checks/README.md).
At least one _layout file exists -- the skill's rule: ALWAYS use _layout.tsx to define stacks

Anti-pattern the skill calls out by name: never co-locate components/types/utilities in the app directory. This is a denylist heuristic, not exhaustive -- it can miss the anti-pattern under an unlisted name, and could in principle false-positive if an app has a genuine *route* literally named one of these (not observed in any real app checked so far).
components/ (or src/components/) exists for reusable UI
Anti-pattern: the skill says colocate StyleSheet.create in the component file, not a separate *.styles.ts file
Anti-pattern: the skill prefers colocated x.test.ts beside x.ts over a __tests__/ folder
Shared by expo-router and expo-project-structure: tsconfig.json (or jsconfig.json) compilerOptions.paths configures the '@/*' alias both skills prefer over relative imports.

expo-router rule: kebab-case file names in app/, no special characters (which includes no uppercase letters). Route-group names like (tabs), dynamic segments like [id], and _layout/index are all lowercase already, so this only flags a genuine PascalCase/camelCase route filename.

expo-router rule: a route group can never be a file named (foo).tsx -- it must be a (foo)/index.tsx directory. Distinct from router_no_colocated_non_route_files_in_app_dir (that's about non-route files under a denylisted name, this is about the illegal group-as-file shape).
expo-router convention: a +not-found route for unmatched paths.
expo-native-ui rule: expo-av is removed -- use expo-audio/expo-video instead.
expo-native-ui rule: use useWindowDimensions, not Dimensions.get().

expo-native-ui rule: use react-native-safe-area-context, not react-native's own SafeAreaView. Anchored to the import statement (not a bare word match) to avoid flagging the correct import from react-native-safe-area-context.

Actually imports from @expo/ui (root, a platform-specific subpackage, or a community drop-in), not just declares it as a package.json dependency. A dependency-only check (an earlier version of this check) has a real loophole: an app can declare @expo/ui and never import or render anything from it, and still pass every expo-ui check, since the other two are absence checks -- confirmed live against both real hot_chocolate/wiki_reader apps, which declare the dependency but never import it anywhere in src/.
expo-ui rule: Host must always be imported from the '@expo/ui' root, never from a platform-specific subpackage.
expo-ui rule: platform-specific @expo/ui trees must live in components/, never under app/ -- Expo Router doesn't support platform extensions for route files.
expo-data-fetching rule: avoid axios, prefer the built-in fetch (or expo/fetch).
expo-data-fetching rule: real network requests use fetch directly, or a proper data-fetching library (React Query, SWR) for anything non-trivial.
expo-tailwind-setup rule: nativewind is a declared dependency.
expo-tailwind-setup rule: tailwindcss is a declared dependency.
expo-tailwind-setup rule: metro.config.js must wrap its config with withNativewind(...).

expo-tailwind-setup rule: postcss.config.mjs uses the official @tailwindcss/postcss plugin. Checked as a text match rather than path_exists on postcss.config.mjs alone, since postcss.config.mjs is read as source (.mjs is a SOURCE_SUFFIXES extension) and this also confirms the right plugin, not just any postcss config file.

expo-tailwind-setup rule: a global.css importing the tailwind theme/preflight/utilities exists. Existence-only -- CSS file content isn't part of the source corpus any lexical check reads, so this can't confirm the actual @import lines.

expo-app-clip rule: an App Clip target is scaffolded at targets/clip/ via @bacons/apple-targets. Config-subset check only -- see SKILL_UPTAKE_COVERAGE_ANALYSIS.md for why the fuller app.json/AASA-content rules aren't checked here.

expo-app-clip rule: the Apple App Site Association file is hosted at .well-known/apple-app-site-association. Existence-only, not content-verified (needs its appclips/webcredentials/activitycontinuation blocks for real correctness, deferred).
